1. (Currently Amended) A golf tee comprising a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, said tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, said member surrounding said shaft and being located below said ball support end and having an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect said support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from said tee, and wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a material that provides greater durability against impacts. 

2. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 2, wherein said tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member, and wherein said material is a high strength synthetic polymer.

3. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of wood, metal, and plastic, wherein said wood is a hardwood and combinations of these materials.

4. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 5, wherein said tee is formed from an engineering plastic that enhances the structural integrity of the shaft and withstands stress during use.

5. (Cancelled) (Claim 6) 

6. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 7, wherein said tee is formed from a flexible nylon material that provides resilience during impacts.

7. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 8, wherein said tee is formed from a malleable metal alloy that improves the durability while maintaining lightweight characteristics.

8. (Cancelled) (Claim 9) 

9. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 10, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a viscoelastic material comprising a natural or man-made polymer that provides enhanced shock absorption.

10. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising an engineered polymer or composite that provides enhanced impact resistance.

11. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 12, wherein said force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer, chosen for improved shock absorption characteristics.

12. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 13, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene or similar elastomer having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer.

13. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 14, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene or an equivalent elastomer.

14. (Currently Amended) A method of making a golf tee for use when striking a golf ball, said method comprising the step of forming a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, the tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, wherein the member surrounding the shaft is located below the ball support end and has an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect the support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from the tee, and wherein the tee is formed from a high strength material that enhances durability.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 16, wherein the tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member, and wherein the material is a high strength synthetic polymer.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of wood, metal, and plastic, wherein said wood is a hardwood or said metal is selected to enhance durability.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 19, wherein the tee is formed from an engineering plastic that provides flexibility and reduces the risk of fracture.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 20, wherein the tee is formed from a polycarbonate or an alternative composite material that provides impact resistance.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21, wherein the tee is formed from nylon, selected for its resilience during use.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 22, wherein the tee is formed from a malleable metal alloy that improves durability while maintaining a lightweight structure.

21. (Cancelled) (Claim 23)

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 24, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a resilient material comprising a natural or man-made polymer that enhances impact absorption.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a material that provides shock absorption and protection for the golf tee.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 26, wherein the force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer, and is selected to provide optimal shock absorption.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 27, wherein the force absorbing material comprises a neoprene having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer, providing enhanced impact resistance.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 28, wherein the force absorbing material comprises neoprene or a similar elastomer exhibiting durability and flexibility.
